name: Himalaya Nutravedics India Limited
sector: Ayurveda and nutraceutical manufacturing / own-brand marketing
research_status: Deep research completed with material evidence holds
identity_note: Not affiliated with Himalaya Wellness or Himalaya Global Holdings. BSE544943; official interop security master is not evidence of NSE listing.
summary:
Research hold, not a favorable investment classification. Himalaya Nutravedics India Limited is a recently listed BSE SME manufacturer and marketer, not Himalaya Wellness. The two must not be combined for brand strength, operating history or ownership. At the corroborated secondary 19 October 2026 close of ₹134.35, issued capital implies ₹118.31 crore market value. The actual lot-aware reference position is 3600 shares, ₹483660 before costs, rather than an impossible exact ₹5 lakh holding. [S1][M1][M2][M3]

The positive case is real reported scaling: FY26 revenue ₹43.0675 crore, EBITDA ₹8.1034 crore and a much larger own-brand contribution. The decisive counterweight is three consecutive negative operating-cash years, customer/supplier concentration and a live trademark dispute that can affect the brand plan. Separately, the original FY23 tax computation and subsequent IPO tax/MAT presentation need a material election-validity reconciliation. This is an unresolved question, not a legal or fraud conclusion. [S1][S3][S4]

BQS, GQS and IAS are all NS because capital-return attribution, current funding and tradability evidence remain incomplete. GQS means Growth Quality Score, not generic growth potential. CASH 3 imposes a ceiling 5, but a ceiling is not a score. Ordinary five-year returns and entry prices are null; the base illustration has 12.91% conditional annual return before execution costs, below the 15% hurdle, and is not actionable. Overall confidence for an investment conclusion is Low.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff 20 October 2026; valuation observation 19 October 2026; exact five-year horizon 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; nominal equity hurdle 15% before investor taxes, fees and execution slippage unless a sensitivity explicitly adds them. Financial units are ₹crore, per-share figures ₹, and capacity units are separately labeled. The legal entity is Himalaya Nutravedics India Limited, ISIN INE 1 OTR 01013, BSE 544943/HNIL. Incorporation 16 June 2022 and operations from September 2022 constrain usable history. Standalone is the appropriate perimeter because the prospectus says no holding/subsidiary/associate; an unrelated brand group must not be consolidated. [S1][M1]

G1 Conditional: no substantiated minority diversion was found, but the record is short. G2 Hold: tax presentation/election-validity reconciliation is materially unresolved. G3 Hold: post-IPO available funds and facility rollover are not verified. G4 Hold: short, partly secondary trading history does not meet the complete liquidity test. None is called Fail simply because evidence is missing. [S1][S3][S4][S10][S11]

Confidence is High for source-transcribed historical totals, Medium for reported operating mix and governance interpretation, Low for tax reconciliation/current funding and execution. Retrieval on 21 October does not extend the decision cutoff: later market observations are excluded. Current webpages establish historical disclosures only; no post-cutoff corporate event is used. Missing interim accounts are ND, pre-incorporation years NA, and unscoreable factors NS, never fabricated zeros.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Primitive factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4 and L NS. Each has supporting and contrary evidence in the 13-factor audit. REV uses a clearly disclosed two-full-year short-history exception because a comparable three- or five-year period does not exist; its schedule score 9 is capped 8, with no trajectory bonus and no second arbitrary small-base deduction. [S1][S3]

Exact Decimal BQS known contribution 3.96 at 80% coverage leaves raw mathematical bounds 4.16–5.96. GQS known 5.25 at 85% coverage leaves raw bounds 5.40–6.75; applying the persistent CASH 3 ceiling gives 5.00–5.00 cap-adjusted bounds, yet its point remains NS. IAS known 1.00 at 30% coverage gives primitive missing-data bounds 1.70–8.00; propagating the available BQS interval narrows them to 2.49–6.99. Neither interval is a probability distribution, confidence interval or rank. Q is final BQS divided by nothing: it remains on the same 1–10 scale, and missing Q cannot be substituted with a midpoint.

Formula weights, each factor contribution, missing weights and override status are embedded. A one-point judgment shift changes BQS by.08–.20, GQS by.10–.40 and IAS direct factors by.10–.35, but no sensitivity cures missing evidence. No undisclosed haircut or governance override is imposed; the evidence-supported research hold is separate from arithmetic.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The issuer makes Ayurveda/nutraceutical products in softgel, oil, tablet and other forms, sells its own brands and manufactures for third parties. FY26 own-brand revenue ₹22.0254 crore is 51.14% of sales, versus ₹4.1249 crore in FY25; contract business rose from ₹16.8716 crore to ₹21.0421 crore. That is a shift in commercial mix, not proof that retail customers independently prefer or repeatedly buy the new brands. Revenue is recognized on reported commercial sales; consumer sell-through and returns data are not independently established. [S1][S6]

FY26 softgel revenue ₹25.7261 crore and oils ₹12.8914 crore dominate; tablets ₹3.3116 crore and others ₹1.1384 crore are smaller. Softgel output 76.465 million units is about 63.72% of reported 120 million capacity. Oil output 811870 bottles versus 900000 capacity is about 90.21%; tablet output 8.029 million versus 45 million is 17.84%. Products, pack sizes and formulation economics differ, so aggregating these units or assuming tablet slack can fill oil demand is inappropriate. [S1]

The company reported a 17-state reach and 58 sales staff by July 2026, but about 49.33% FY26 sales originated in Kerala and third-party sales were even more geographically concentrated. Customer purchasing, repeat orders, distributor inventory and supplier reliability therefore matter more than a large national market forecast. The company has no verified long-term volume commitments, and no clinical efficacy or therapeutic advantage is assumed in this research.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
A useful manufacturing base, formulation know-how and customer relationships can reduce a buyer’s onboarding friction. These are possible service/cost advantages, not yet durable pricing power. The largest customer represented 36.02% of FY26 sales and the top 10 represented 81.24%; one supplier represented 62.13% and the top 10 suppliers 94.30%. This leaves bargaining power concentrated on both sides. Concentration improved versus FY25 customers, a positive fact, but no long-term contract protects renewal. [S1]

The corporate name cannot inherit Himalaya Wellness’s brand history or recognition. The prospectus explicitly disclaims affiliation, describes opposed marks and says the company would stop new packing under an opposed corporate logo while transitioning inventory. The 4 October suit seeks broader relief, while the company contests it. Neither an allegation nor an issuer denial establishes the final legal outcome. The risk is commercial interruption and additional marketing/relabeling costs, not a claimed adverse court ruling. [S1][S4]

Peer economics provide perspective without false comparability. Sandu’s FY26 sales ₹69.9345 crore and PAT ₹1.7662 crore illustrate that established Ayurveda manufacturing does not necessarily produce very high margins. Jeena Sikho’s ₹801.3639 crore consolidated revenue includes hospitals/services, unlike this issuer. Dabur’s ₹13193 crore diversified consumer franchise is a scale/brand benchmark, not an acceptable automatic valuation multiple. No market-share leadership, proprietary medical effectiveness, protected patent portfolio or audited customer lifetime value was verified. MOAT 4 reflects commercial capability with replicable features and weak evidence of durability.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The comparable restated series is ₹14.4256 crore FY24, ₹20.9965 crore FY25 and ₹43.0675 crore FY26. Growth is 45.55% and 105.12%, with absolute additions ₹6.5709 crore and ₹22.0710 crore. Two-year CAGR is 72.79%. Three-, five- and ten-year comparable CAGR remain null. The original startup FY23 sales ₹2.0460 crore cover about seven operating months; mechanically annualizing or treating that as a full-year base would distort scoring. [S1][S3]

Softgel units rose 34.525 million to 40.748 million to 76.465 million; oil units 90000 to 507725 to 811870. Volumes therefore support underlying expansion, although selling prices, pack sizes and mix mean revenue growth cannot be called purely organic constant-price demand. No acquisition contribution is disclosed, but the absence of an acquisition is not the same as independently verified brand sell-through. Own-brand sales grew more than fivefold in FY26, explaining much of the acceleration; the contract base grew much more slowly. [S1]

The bottom-up ceiling is product-specific. More softgel utilization offers room, whereas oil is already near the stated capacity ceiling and may need equipment, labor, quality systems or a different mix. New geographies require distributor economics and cash funding. The IPO working-capital/branding plan does not itself expand manufacturing capacity. Revenue remains tiny relative to national categories, but addressable market size is not evidence this company can win profitable share. There are no verified FY27 comparable interims or TTM figures in this record.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth quality is constrained by its cash requirement. FY24–26 cumulative CFO is ₹−5.7765 crore against ₹10.0475 crore PAT, or-0.5749 x. Cash capex totals ₹1.3604 crore and free-cash-flow proxy is ₹−7.1369 crore, before financing interest. Inventory and receivables, not heavy fixed-asset spending, absorbed most new funds. This is why CASH 3 is a persistent realization judgment rather than a transient capex penalty. [S1]

The operating invested-capital bridge includes receivables, inventory, operating advances/prepayments and GST claims, less operating payables/provisions, plus operating fixed assets. Cash, investments, MAT credits, IPO deferrals and tax accounts are separately reconciled rather than called productive incremental capital. Operating IC rises about ₹4.3905 crore to ₹8.4240 crore to ₹19.4693 crore. ROIC and an incremental book-capital proxy can be calculated, but profit attribution to a newly funded product/customer cohort, its ramp costs and maintenance capital are absent. CAP is therefore NS even though aggregate returns look strong. [S1]

The planned ₹13.75 crore working-capital allocation and ₹7.5 crore branding spend could enable growth if inventories sell and customers pay. Neither allocation proves high-return reinvestment. The model expenses campaigns and retainer, treats working-capital investment through changes in operating balances, and does not subtract the same earmarked IPO amount again. The next evidence should be sell-through, collections, contribution after marketing and cohort payback, not a repeat of the market-size claim. GQS remains NS, subject to ceiling 5.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter-led execution has delivered a larger manufacturing and own-brand operation in a short time. The final prospectus reports promoters 5512500 shares/62.60% post-IPO and promoter plus promoter group 6000000 shares/68.13%; it states no pledge and no outstanding warrants/options/convertibles. These are prospectus-date pro forma statements, not a separately authenticated October holding/encumbrance filing. FY26 remuneration disclosed for Rohit Asawa and Sneha Penmatsa totals ₹.3040 crore; related director loans show nil closing balances in FY25 and FY26. Large historical loan movements require attention, but a disclosed loan repayment is not automatically leakage. No unsupported allegation of related-party abuse is made. [S1]

The prior auditor resigned in November 2025 and a peer-reviewed firm was appointed later that month. The issuer explains this in the context of IPO preparedness. This is a disclosed auditor change, not proof of coercion or an adverse resignation; unmodified audit opinions are retained. Original-to-restated PAT changes are explicitly reconciled, without adding an adjustment subtotal twice to its components. Nonetheless, unmodified wording cannot substitute for a specific explanation of the original 115BAA computation versus later 80-IAC/MAT treatment. [S1][S3][S9]

The 4 October suit was disclosed promptly in the reviewed issuer letter. Its claimants allege trademark infringement/passing off and seek financial and injunctive relief; the company strongly denies the claims. The 17 October price-query response says there is no undisclosed material event and price movements are market-driven. These are attributed statements, not proof that the exchange cleared financial reliability or the courts ruled favorably. [S4][S5]

Operational execution deserves credit for output and mix expansion, but marketing ROI, creditor/facility continuity and collections are unverified. EXEC 5 and GOV 5 reflect this mixed evidence. A short listed history also leaves capital-allocation discipline over a full cycle untested.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 EBITDA ₹8.1034 crore less depreciation ₹.3254 crore gives EBIT ₹7.7780 crore. After finance ₹.3495 crore and other income ₹.0528 crore, PBT is ₹7.4813 crore; PAT ₹7.3897 crore reflects only ₹.0916 crore net tax charge. A 25.17% analytical normal-tax rate on operating pretax income gives ₹5.5587 crore normalized PAT, rather than assuming permanent near-zero taxes. Other income is small and does not explain the operating improvement. [S1]

The key reliability question is tax election history. Original FY23 computation PDF 3 uses section 115BAA and says MAT does not apply; Form3CD PDF 27 item 8 a marks the 115BAA option Yes. Later restatement claims 80-IAC deductions and recognizes ₹1.6229 crore MAT credit. Official 115BAA text conditions the concession on specified exclusions, makes a valid election persistent, and also provides an invalidation mechanism if conditions are not met. The computation and Form3CD report the position but do not themselves establish a valid Form 10-IC filing or what changed later. Actual election/invalidation and auditor reconciliation were not found. G2 is Hold, not a finding of illegal tax treatment. The separate FY25 deduction-timing dispute and ₹.272597 crore demand are disclosed; the appeal was pending in the prospectus. [S1][S3][S10][S11]

FY26 cash generated before working capital ₹8.1094 crore is overwhelmed by inventory ₹5.6313 crore and receivables ₹4.9474 crore absorption; the full CFO bridge preserves MAT, provisions and the reported tax-paid line. Restricted deposits ₹.9994 crore are excluded from ₹1.4454 crore gross cash, leaving ₹.4460 crore available. Current-share EPS ₹8.3914 differs from historical weighted EPS 12.05. The bonus-adjusted FY25 EPS 16.54 already shows why PAT growth is not equivalent to owner-per-share compounding. Missing cash-flow details in startup FY23 remain ND, not zero.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹134.35 and 8806320 shares, market capitalization is ₹118.3129 crore, historical reported FY26 P/E 16.01 x and normal-tax operating P/E 21.28 x. Current enterprise value is null because an audited/verified October post-IPO cash/debt bridge is unavailable. Adding the entire IPO gross cash to historical equity, ignoring fees and operating burn, would manufacture cheapness. A historical EV illustration is labeled as such and cannot become a live EV. [S1][M1][M2][M3]

The annual/stub model runs exactly 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with FY27 remaining 163 days, full FY28–31 and the final FY32 October stub. Brand and contract sales have separate drivers; margins, marketing, tax, working capital, capex, debt service, cash floor and diluted shares reconcile every period. Conditional bear/base/bull terminal values are ₹19.51/₹246.58/₹555.53 per share. Their non-rescue conditional annual returns are-32.02%/12.91%/32.83%. These are assumption tests, not expected or ordinary returns; all ordinary IRR and entry-price fields remain null. Severe floor-breach paths also have null non-rescue conditional returns. [S1][S4]

Base uses declining brand growth 35% toward 12%, contract 15% toward 5%,18% operating margin before incremental campaigns,94 receivable days and 100 inventory days, plus 3% sales capex. The model retains operating cash at exit, never distributes restricted deposits, and neither adds operating property to enterprise value nor values MAT credits separately. FCFF DCF tests 14–20% WACC,3–5% terminal growth and 20% terminal ROIC; terminal operating reinvestment, separate terminal cash-reserve growth and explicit-period cash-floor changes are funded. Reverse hurdle and growth/multiple/collection sensitivities disclose fixed-balance assumptions rather than pretending to solve self-funding growth.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The linked bear combines a sharp brand/contract decline, lower margins, longer collection and inventory cycles, legal/relabeling cash costs and full repayment of the callable cash-credit balance. It is not merely a smaller exit multiple. It retains operating cash needs and existing tax obligations, then values only the remaining owner claim. Conditional bear terminal price ₹19.51 is about 85.48% below the entry reference. That is a modeled economic impairment path, not a prediction of a court ruling or a price target. [S1][S4]

An additional severe branch stretches receivables to 270 days and inventory to 300 days while the credit line is called. It creates a peak required cash gap ₹11.06 crore. Its non-rescue conditional return and entries are null from the first required-floor breach: continuing an unfunded company as if it survived would be misleading. A separate equity-rescue experiment issues whole shares at a 50% price discount, charges 3% issuance fees and recalculates dilution. It is neither committed funding nor an ordinary return available to today’s holder.

The cash claim from litigation is not bounded by the ₹2.0001 crore specified damages alone: costs, profit rendition and potential injunction/business disruption are separately uncertain. Conversely, the company denies the claim and no adverse order was reported as of 4 October; no later order is invented. The IPO can materially help solvency if proceeds remain available, and customer concentration has improved. These counterfacts prevent a false default or Fail conclusion. The principal failure mechanism is a joint cash-conversion/legal/funding shock, not just market volatility.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A 5× price outcome requires 37.97% annual compounding over five years;10× requires 58.49%. Over ten years the corresponding rates are 17.46% and 25.89%. These are return arithmetic, not evidence that the company can achieve them. At a 12× terminal P/E and 12% net margin with no new dilution,5× requires about ₹410.81 crore sales and 10× about ₹821.62 crore, compared with FY26 ₹43.0675 crore. [S1][M1][M2]

Those revenue levels require new distribution, customer diversification, substantially more productive capacity or a different product mix, and very large working-capital funding unless collection economics improve. Oil is already near reported capacity; existing tablet slack does not solve the same bottleneck. A forecast that holds historical high reported PAT margin forever ignores tax normalization and campaign costs. A forecast that pays for growth with new shares must reduce the old holder’s ownership, even if company profits grow.

The required evidence is multiple years of positive cash after maintenance investment, independently supportable incremental returns, brand continuity and repeat customer economics. A huge category TAM and a low starting revenue base do not substitute for that evidence. Classification is Speculative/unsupported for multibagger claims, not a compounder designation. The bull case is a conditional illustration and does not validate 5× or 10× promises.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First priority is the tax reconciliation: valid Form 10-IC election status or documented invalidation, the bridge to subsequent 80-IAC/MAT treatment, the legal/tax basis for recoverability of the ₹1.6229 crore MAT asset, and the FY25 appeal outcome. A management explanation should be matched to the underlying document or signed auditor/tax reconciliation; a landing-page label or search snippet does not satisfy this request. [S1][S3][S10][S11]

Second, obtain a dated post-IPO deployment and bank reconciliation: net cash actually received, unpaid issue expenses, remaining restricted deposits, actual brand/campaign spending and bank facility terms. Track actual receivable collections against ₹10.5869 crore closing FY26 receivables, inventory conversion against ₹8.9154 crore, cash tax payments and operating cash after required capex. Quarterly revenue alone does not clear G3. Observe whether customer concentration falls without distributor inventory rising. [S1]

Third, track the trademark case through authenticated orders, not inferred victory from a jurisdictional return or issuer denial. Map any name/label transition to inventory write-offs, rebranding cost, distributor acceptance and revenue continuity. Compare actual marketing contribution with the ₹7.5 crore proposed spend plus internal retainer. [S1][S4]

Fourth, build sufficient authenticated BSE trading history and verify contemporary lot, price-band, queue and two-sided depth. At 19 October the reference position is 3 lots, not fractional shares. Improvement triggers are sustained positive CFO, collection days near or below the modeled base, no unresolved tax discrepancy and demonstrable funding without rescue. Deterioration triggers are aging concentration, inventory/write-offs, adverse injunction, additional dilution or loss of banking support. No external monitor or trading action is implied by this plan.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final research status: deep-research dossier completed with material unresolved evidence, not a completed favorable investment case. Business quality NS, Growth Quality NS with ceiling 5, Investment Attractiveness NS. G1 Conditional; G2, G3 and G4 Hold. Risk is High; investment-conclusion confidence Low. The company is not designated a compounder, and no positive ranked placement is appropriate while the necessary evidence is missing. A short operating history is not an automatic rejection, but high growth cannot override material financial reliability or financing gaps.

For a new-investment research decision, defer an actionable price or return conclusion until the tax election/reliability question and actual post-IPO funding are reconciled, then re-run the full share-aware model at a newly authenticated quote. For an existing holder, practical lot/queue risk and the cash/legal failure path matter; this dossier does not infer the holder’s cost basis, financial needs or authorization to trade. No buy/sell instruction is given.

The base conditional return below 15% is useful as a falsifiable assumption test, but the stronger reason for the hold is evidence quality, not a precise valuation target. If collections improve, unused proceeds are verified, tax treatment is reconciled and a branded cash-generative business persists, BQS/GQS/IAS can be reconsidered under the same rubric. If evidence proves severe misconduct or actual unfinanceable default, gates should change on that evidence, not by converting uncertainty into a fabricated low factor today.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source register identifies actual documents, publication dates when verified, locators, source hierarchy, retrieval date, authentication limits and SHA 256 hashes. The prospectus and issuer-hosted accounts are primary issuer documents; suit and price-query letters were read as actual PDFs through a public mirror because direct BSE attachment access was blocked. Mirror retrieval is not claimed to cryptographically authenticate an inaccessible exchange original. The official security master supports identity/capital/lot, not BSE historical traded value. Two secondary tables corroborate the 19 October close and volume. [S1–S11][M1–M3]

Raw issuer PDFs, OCR, page images, public financial-account identifiers and personal identifiers are excluded from portable research packages. Safe financial extracts, analyst calculations, reproducible code, results, source URLs and hashes remain. Such a package can reproduce calculations but cannot independently reauthenticate omitted originals without retrieving them again. A source landing page is never described as a document, approval or certificate that was not opened.

Main open questions are the tax election and MAT reconciliation; FY27 interim financials; actual October unrestricted cash and IPO deployment; demand-facility terms/current availability; customer collections and returns; brand transition/court outcome; attributable incremental returns; and authenticated tradability. Analyst assumptions are separate from verified history and management statements. All normal-tax, growth, margin, working-capital, capex, legal cost, multiple and rescue settings are exposed in the model. Results are research scenarios, not investment, tax or legal advice and not an instruction or authority to trade.
